doctor.title: finitemonkey doctor ({version})
doctor.summary: {ok} ok, {warn, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}}, {fail, plural, one {# failure} other {# failures}}
doctor.node.old: Node.js {version} is older than the minimum {min}
doctor.node.fix: Install Node.js 20 or newer from https://nodejs.org
doctor.git.old: git {version} is older than {min}; some commands will need a newer git
doctor.claude.missing: Claude Code was not found; the CLI works without it, the hooks need it
doctor.claude.fix_timeout: Run `claude --version` by hand and check that it answers
doctor.path.plain: Project path has no spaces or accents
doctor.path.chars: Project path has spaces or accents: {path}
doctor.path.fix_chars: Finite Monkey handles this path; if another tool fails here, move the project to a path without spaces or accents
doctor.path.synced: Project is inside a synced folder (OneDrive, Dropbox, iCloud or Google Drive): {path}
doctor.path.fix_synced: Move the project out of the synced folder to avoid sync conflicts and slow git
doctor.path.wsl_mount: Project is on a Windows drive mounted in WSL: {path}
doctor.path.fix_wsl_mount: Move the project into the Linux home (for example ~/projects) for faster git and correct permissions
doctor.node.unsupported: Node.js {version} stopped getting security fixes on {date}
doctor.node.fix_unsupported: Install a supported Node.js LTS from https://nodejs.org
doctor.claude.old: Claude Code {version} is older than {min}; a guard that crashes lets the action through instead of blocking it
doctor.sandbox.ok: The Claude Code sandbox can run on this system
doctor.sandbox.windows: Native Windows has no Claude Code sandbox; commands run with your full permissions
doctor.sandbox.fix_windows: Use Claude Code inside WSL 2: wsl --install
doctor.sandbox.missing: The Claude Code sandbox cannot run here: missing {tools}
doctor.sandbox.fix_missing: Install the tools: sudo apt-get install bubblewrap socat (or your distribution's equivalent)
doctor.path.copies: {count, plural, one {# copy} other {# copies}} of finitemonkey on PATH; the first one wins, and it may be an old version: {paths}
doctor.path.fix_copies: Keep one: npm uninstall -g finitemonkey, and use the copy the project installs
doctor.auth.env: {names} set in the shell; Claude Code switches account or endpoint when it sees them
doctor.auth.fix_env: If that was not on purpose, remove them from the shell profile and run: {command}
doctor.settings.disable_all_hooks: disableAllHooks is on ({scopes}); no Finite Monkey hook runs
doctor.settings.fix_disable_all_hooks: Remove "disableAllHooks" from the settings file of that scope, or run /hooks in Claude Code to turn hooks back on
doctor.settings.managed_hooks_only: allowManagedHooksOnly is on ({scopes}); Claude Code ignores the hooks in the project settings
doctor.settings.fix_managed_hooks_only: Ask the administrator of the managed settings to add the Finite Monkey hooks there, or to turn allowManagedHooksOnly off
doctor.settings.plugin_only: strictPluginOnlyCustomization is on ({scopes}) and the finitemonkey plugin is not enabled; the project hooks do not load
doctor.settings.fix_plugin_only: Install the plugin: finitemonkey init --marketplace --yes, then /plugin install finitemonkey@finitemonkey in Claude Code
doctor.settings.plugin_channels: Both {stable} and {next} are enabled. They share the plugin name, so Claude Code keeps only one set of hooks
doctor.settings.fix_plugin_channels: To stay on stable run claude plugin disable {next}; to test next run claude plugin disable {stable}
doctor.settings.agent_teams: {name} is on; teammates run in their own sessions, and Finite Monkey does not check their work before they report done
doctor.settings.fix_agent_teams: Run `finitemonkey gate` before accepting a teammate's result, or unset the variable
doctor.settings.loop_plugins: {names} enabled: it sends the agent back to work at Stop, and its loop has no guard of its own
doctor.settings.fix_loop_plugins: Disable it in this project with /plugin in Claude Code, or keep it and let the Finite Monkey Stop hook decide
doctor.settings.cleanup_period: cleanupPeriodDays is {days}, but the project is {age, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} old; Claude Code deletes session transcripts before the history they explain
doctor.settings.fix_cleanup_period: Raise "cleanupPeriodDays" in ~/.claude/settings.json to at least the age of the project
doctor.instructions.claudeignore: {file} has no effect in Claude Code; these deny rules are missing: {rules}
doctor.instructions.fix_claudeignore: Run `finitemonkey update --yes` (or `finitemonkey init` on a new project) to add them to .claude/settings.json
doctor.instructions.denied: A Read deny rule hides instruction files from the agent: {files}
doctor.instructions.fix_denied: Narrow the matching Read rule in permissions.deny so it no longer covers AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules
doctor.instructions.local: CLAUDE.local.md exists; it loads only on this machine and can override AGENTS.md without anyone else seeing it
doctor.instructions.fix_local: Move the rules the team needs into AGENTS.md, then delete CLAUDE.local.md
doctor.instructions.size: {file} has {lines, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}, above the ceiling of {max}; long instruction files get followed less
doctor.instructions.fix_size: Move detail into .claude/rules or linked docs until the file is under the ceiling
doctor.instructions.duplicated: {count, plural, one {# rule line repeats} other {# rule lines repeat}} across AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules, for example: "{example}"
doctor.instructions.fix_duplicated: Keep each rule in one file; copies drift apart and then contradict each other
doctor.project.lockfiles: More than one {ecosystem} lockfile: {files}; installs depend on which tool runs
doctor.project.fix_lockfiles: Keep the lockfile of the package manager the project uses and delete the others with git rm
doctor.project.configs: More than one {tool} config file: {files}; only one of them is read
doctor.project.fix_configs: Merge them into one file and delete the rest with git rm
doctor.hooks.timeout: {source} {event} hook gave no answer within {ms} ms: {command}
doctor.hooks.output: {source} {event} hook did not print a JSON answer: {detail}
doctor.hooks.fix_broken: Run `finitemonkey update --yes` to register it again; if it still fails, run it by hand to see the error: {command}
doctor.hooks.fix_broken_plugin: Reinstall the plugin: claude plugin uninstall finitemonkey@finitemonkey, then claude plugin install finitemonkey@finitemonkey
doctor.hooks.slow: {source} {event} hook took {ms} ms; Claude Code waits for it on every call
doctor.hooks.fix_slow: Install finitemonkey in the project (npm install -D finitemonkey) so the hook skips npx, then run `finitemonkey update --yes`
doctor.hooks.fail_open: {source} {event} guard is registered without onFailure "block"; if it crashes, Claude Code lets the action through
doctor.hooks.fix_fail_open: Update Claude Code to {min} or newer (claude update), then run `finitemonkey update --yes`
doctor.hooks.fix_matcher: Run `finitemonkey update --yes` to register the guard for every tool
doctor.hooks.not_fired: {source} {event} hook not fired: it runs finitemonkey {found} and this doctor is {version}
doctor.hooks.fix_not_fired: Run `npx finitemonkey@{found} doctor` to test it, or `npx finitemonkey@{version} update --yes` to move the hooks to this version
doctor.hooks.schema: {file} does not match the hooks schema of Claude Code {claude}: {problems}
doctor.hooks.fix_schema: Fix those fields, or run `finitemonkey update --yes` to rewrite the Finite Monkey entries; for the plugin, reinstall it with claude plugin install finitemonkey@finitemonkey
doctor.hooks.plugin_disabled: The finitemonkey plugin is disabled in the {scope} settings; its hooks do not run
doctor.hooks.fix_plugin_disabled: Turn it back on: claude plugin enable finitemonkey@finitemonkey
doctor.hooks.none: No Finite Monkey hook is registered for this project
doctor.hooks.absent: Finite Monkey is installed, but no hook is registered for: {events}
doctor.hooks.fix_absent: Run `finitemonkey update --yes` (or `finitemonkey doctor --fix`) to register them again
doctor.hooks.version_ok: Hooks and this doctor run finitemonkey {version}
doctor.hooks.version_plugin: The project hooks run finitemonkey {project}, but the plugin is {plugin}
doctor.hooks.fix_version_plugin: Align the project with the plugin: npx finitemonkey@{plugin} update --yes
doctor.hooks.version_cli: The hooks run finitemonkey {found}, but this doctor is {version}
doctor.hooks.fix_version_cli: Move the hooks to this version: npx finitemonkey@{version} update --yes
doctor.hooks.fix_version_cli_plugin: Update the plugin: claude plugin update finitemonkey@finitemonkey
doctor.fix.not_installed: --fix: Finite Monkey is not installed in this project, so there is nothing to repair; run `npx finitemonkey init`
doctor.fix.manual: --fix does not touch user settings, the shell profile or the system; run the fix shown under each remaining item
doctor.report.written: Report written to {path}; attach it to the issue
hook.failed_closed: the {event} hook could not run ({detail}), so it blocked to stay safe. Run `finitemonkey doctor`
hook.failed_open: the {event} hook could not run ({detail}); continuing without it. Run `finitemonkey doctor`
exit.ok: 0 ok: the command did what it was asked
exit.check_failed: 1 check failed: the command ran and found a problem
exit.usage: 2 usage error: unknown command, unknown flag, bad value or command not available yet
exit.not_configured: 3 not configured: setup or a prerequisite (node, git, files, permissions) is missing
exit.needs_person: 4 needs a person: a decision or approval is required before going on
exit.internal: 5 internal error: Finite Monkey itself failed; please report it
hook.stop_released: the {event} hook would block again ({detail}), but Claude Code is already continuing from a stop hook, so it lets the session stop. Run `finitemonkey doctor`
error.needs_confirmation: "{command}" needs your decision before it changes anything: {question}

secrets.command.accept: Accept one finding into the baseline, with a reason and an expiry (the person only)
secrets.command.incident: List secret incidents, mark them rotated or closed, and show the history purge steps
secrets.block.write.claim: the new text for {file} has a credential ({found})
secrets.block.write.requires: Nothing was written. Keep the value in .env (outside git) and read it by its variable name. If the key is real, treat it as exposed and rotate it
secrets.block.not: an encoded, split, commented or renamed copy of the same value
secrets.block.human: Kept a credential out of a file, command or commit.
secrets.block.bash.claim: this command has a credential ({found}) and did not run
secrets.block.bash.requires: Read the value from an environment variable instead of writing it in the command. If the key is real, treat it as exposed and rotate it
secrets.block.commit.claim: the staged changes have a credential ({found}), so the commit did not run
secrets.block.commit.requires: Remove it from the staged files, keep it in .env (outside git) and rotate it if it is real
secrets.block.read.claim: {target} holds secrets, and reading it would put their values in the conversation
secrets.block.read.requires: Ask the person for the variable names, or read .env.example
secrets.block.env_dump.claim: `{command}` prints every environment variable, secrets included
secrets.block.env_dump.requires: Print only the variable you need by name, or check that it exists with `test -n "$NAME"`
secrets.block.person_only.claim: `{command}` is a decision for the person, not the model
secrets.block.person_only.requires: Ask the person to run it in their own terminal
secrets.block.prompt: your message was not sent to the model: it has a credential ({found}). If this key was pasted anywhere else, treat it as exposed and rotate it. To use it, put it in .env and tell me only the variable name. Never paste keys into the chat. Incident: {incident}.
secrets.post.context: Finite Monkey: the {tool} output contained a credential ({found}). Incident {incident} is open; rotating the key is the person's decision. Finite Monkey output never repeats the value.
secrets.scan.title: Secrets scan ({mode}): {total} found, {new} new, {known} known, {expired} expired, {fixed} fixed
secrets.scan.clean: No secrets found. The monkey keeps its bananas to itself.
secrets.incident.title: {count, plural, one {# incident} other {# incidents}}
secrets.purge.title: History purge for {id} ({where}, first commit {commit}). You run these steps; Finite Monkey never runs them:
secrets.purge.step1: 1. Confirm the old key is revoked at the provider and the new one works in every consumer.
secrets.purge.step2: 2. Outside the repository, write a replacements file with one line per leaked value: <value>==>REMOVED. Copy the value from your own records; Finite Monkey never stores or prints it.
secrets.purge.step3: 3. In a fresh mirror clone, run: git filter-repo --replace-text <replacements file>
secrets.purge.step4: 4. Relax branch protection yourself, push the rewritten refs, restore the protection and tell everyone with a clone to clone again.
secrets.purge.step5: 5. Close the incident: finitemonkey secrets incident close {id}

secrets.error.git_unavailable: The scan could not read git ({detail})

secrets.error.finding_not_found: No current finding has the id {id}
secrets.error.not_rotated: Incident {id} is {state}: rotate the key at the provider first, then mark it rotated

prose.command.check: Check text for patterns readers recognize as machine-written (local only)
prose.rule.opener-routine: open with what happened to someone: a command, a time, an error message
prose.rule.reassurance: cut the consolation line; describe the problem and let the reader judge
prose.rule.slogan-closer: end on a fact or the next step instead of a slogan
prose.rule.rhythmic-triplet: join the short sentences into one that says what each part does
prose.rule.imperative-fragment: replace the loose commands with one sentence about what the product does
prose.rule.antithesis: say what it is; drop the contrast with what it is not
prose.rule.abstract-noun: swap the abstract noun for the scene: who did what, where
prose.rule.crutch-word: use the plain word, or a number that proves the claim
prose.rule.colon-heading: make the heading the question or the task the reader has
prose.rule.decorative-emoji: remove the emoji; the heading carries the meaning
prose.rule.em-dash-series: use a period, a comma or parentheses instead of dashes
prose.warn.command: {target} reads as machine-written ({spans}). Rewrite it before sending. {fixes}. If it is brand text written on purpose, show the person two alternatives.
prose.block.command.claim: {target} reads as machine-written ({spans}), and this project's preset does not send it. {fixes}
prose.block.command.requires: Rewrite it and run the command again
prose.block.not: the same text with a few words swapped
prose.block.human: Held back text that reads as machine-written.
prose.block.unreadable.claim: could not read {file} to check its text ({detail})
prose.block.unreadable.requires: Check the path and run the command again
prose.block.marker.claim: this would add the marker {marker} to {file}, and only the person can add it
prose.block.marker.requires: Rewrite the passage instead, or ask the person to add the marker in their own editor
prose.check.file: {file}: {count, plural, one {# passage that reads} other {# passages that read}} as machine-written
prose.check.allowed: {file}: skipped, the person marked it with {marker}
prose.check.clean: {count, plural, one {# file checked} other {# files checked}}, nothing reads as machine-written. The monkey wrote this one itself.
prose.error.found: {count, plural, one {# passage reads} other {# passages read}} as machine-written
prose.error.no_input: nothing to check: pass files, --stdin, or run it inside a git repository to check the changed Markdown files
prose.block.marker_shell.claim: this command writes the marker {marker}, and only the person can add it
prose.block.marker_shell.requires: Rewrite the passage instead, or ask the person to add the marker in their own editor
prose.rule.requester-reference: state the technical reason for the change; leave out who asked for it
prose.rule.person-as-reason: name the property of the change instead of a person
prose.rule.origin-project: describe the technical property you copied instead of naming where it came from
prose.rule.first-person: write what the change does, in the present tense, without I or you
prose.rule.padding: cut the preamble and start with what changed
gate.require.prose: changed Markdown does not read as machine-written
gate.prose.unavailable: could not read the changed Markdown files (git unavailable)
gate.prose.warning: warning only in this preset: {file}:{line} reads as machine-written ({rules})
gate.prose.clean: {count, plural, one {# changed Markdown file, it does not read} other {# changed Markdown files, none reads}} as machine-written
git.command.snapshot: Save the working tree, index and untracked files to a backup ref without touching them
git.command.undo: List the snapshots or restore one, into a new worktree by default
git.command.rescue: List lost commits from the reflog and fsck, and restore one into a new branch
git.command.merge_verify: Check that a merge kept every change from both sides
git.block.force_push.claim: `{command}` rewrites the remote branch and can erase commits someone else pushed
git.block.force_push.requires: Fetch, integrate the remote commits and push normally. On your own branch after a rebase, use `git push --force-with-lease=<branch>:<expected sha> --force-if-includes`
git.block.not: the same effect through another git command, an alias, a script or a nested shell
git.block.human: Stopped a git command that could lose work or rewrite shared history.
git.block.lease_not_own.claim: `{command}` forces a push onto {subject}, which is not the branch you are working on or is protected
git.block.lease_not_own.requires: A forced push is only for your own branch, with an explicit lease
git.block.push_delete.requires: Deleting a remote branch is for the person to do
git.block.push_mirror.claim: `{command}` overwrites every remote ref and would publish the backup refs
git.block.push_mirror.requires: Push the branch you need by name
git.block.clean.claim: `{command}` deletes untracked files for good; they are in no commit
git.block.clean.requires: Run `git clean -n` to see the list, then move what should go into .finitemonkey/trash/ or ask the person
git.block.stash_drop.claim: `{command}` throws away stashed work that exists nowhere else
git.block.stash_drop.requires: Apply it with `git stash apply` or leave it; dropping a stash is for the person to do
git.block.branch_unmerged.claim: `{command}` deletes {subject}, whose commits are neither in its upstream nor in the default branch
git.block.branch_unmerged.requires: Push or merge it first; `git branch -d` works once it is merged
git.block.worktree_force.claim: `{command}` removes a worktree even with uncommitted changes
git.block.worktree_force.requires: Commit or archive its work first; plain `git worktree remove` refuses a dirty tree on purpose
git.block.rm_worktree.claim: `{command}` deletes {subject}, which is a git worktree or repository; uncommitted work in it would be lost
git.block.rm_worktree.requires: Commit or archive it, then use `git worktree remove` without --force
git.block.rm_root.claim: `{command}` recursively deletes {subject}, a root or home directory
git.block.rm_root.requires: Name the exact folder to remove
git.block.rebase_protected.requires: Change it through a pull request
git.block.rebase_shared.claim: `{command}` rewrites {subject}, which already has someone else's commits on the remote
git.block.rebase_shared.requires: Merge the base into it instead of rebasing
git.block.merge_side.claim: `{command}` resolves conflicts by taking one side whole ({subject}), which silently drops the other side's changes
git.block.merge_side.requires: Resolve each conflict by hand and run `finitemonkey merge verify` before committing
git.block.history.claim: `{command}` deletes history or reflog entries that undo and rescue depend on
git.block.history.requires: Rewriting history is for the person to do
git.block.protected_commit.claim: `{command}` would commit straight onto {subject}, a protected branch
git.block.protected_commit.requires: Create a branch with `git switch -c <type>/<name>` and open a pull request
git.block.protected_push.requires: Push your own branch and open a pull request
git.block.foreign.claim: `{command}` would discard changes this session did not make: {files}
git.block.foreign.requires: Undo only your own lines with Edit
git.block.unknown.claim: `{command}` discards changes, and `git status` failed, so there is no telling whose they are
git.block.unknown.requires: Fix the repository and try again
git.block.snapshot_failed.claim: `{command}` is risky and the safety snapshot before it failed ({detail}), so it did not run
git.block.snapshot_failed.requires: Fix the cause and try again
git.snapshot.context: finitemonkey saved a snapshot before `{command}`: {ref}. `finitemonkey undo {ref}` brings the previous state back.
prod.block.effect.claim: `{command}` changes production ({target}) by hand, and a server edited by hand drifts from the repository
prod.block.effect.requires: Change it through the deploy path ({deploy}): commit, open a pull request and let the deploy run
prod.block.not: the same change through another tool, a script or a nested shell
prod.block.human: Stopped a hand edit to production; changes go through the deploy.
prod.block.interactive.claim: `{command}` opens an interactive session on production ({target}), where nothing typed can be checked first
prod.block.interactive.requires: Run one read-only command at a time, such as `ssh {target} docker ps`
git.undo.list_title: {count, plural, one {# snapshot:} other {# snapshots, newest first:}}
git.undo.worktree: restored {ref} into a new worktree at {path}. Compare it with your tree and copy what you need; `git worktree remove {path}` removes it. The state before this undo is in {backup}.
git.undo.in_place: restored {ref} in place. The state before this undo is in {backup}; `finitemonkey undo {backup}` brings it back.
git.undo.confirm: restoring in place overwrites the working tree and the index. Run it yourself with --in-place --yes to confirm.
git.rescue.title: recovery candidates (read-only, nothing changed):
git.rescue.blobs: {count, plural, one {# staged file content is lost but recoverable} other {# staged file contents are lost but recoverable}}; `git fsck --lost-found` writes them to .git/lost-found/other.
git.rescue.never_staged: a file that was never staged nor committed cannot be recovered from git.
git.merge.ok: nothing lost: {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} checked between {base} and {result}, {justified, plural, one {# justified drop} other {# justified drops}}.
git.merge.lost: {count, plural, one {# change lost} other {# changes lost}} between {base} and {result}:
git.merge.limits: this proves the changes are present, not that the merged code works; the tests of both sides still have to pass.
git.error.merge_lost: {count, plural, one {# change was lost in the merge and is not justified} other {# changes were lost in the merge and are not justified}} in the dropped list.
git.error.merge_unanalyzable: the merge could not be analyzed: {detail}
gate.require.worktree: every file changed in the session committed, and the commits pushed or with a declared destination
gate.require.merge: every merge since the start kept the changes of both sides
gate.worktree.unavailable: could not read the git state of the worktree
gate.worktree.dirty: files changed in this session are not committed: {files}
gate.worktree.unpushed: {count, plural, one {# commit on {branch} exists only on this machine} other {# commits on {branch} exist only on this machine}}
gate.worktree.clean: the session's changes are committed and pushed
gate.merge.unavailable: could not read the merges of the session
gate.merge.clean: {count, plural, one {# merge checked} other {# merges checked}}, nothing lost
doctor.memory.lines: {file}: {lines, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}} of {max}. Edits made during a session apply only after /clear, /compact or a restart.
doctor.memory.too_long: {file}: {lines, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}, above the ceiling of {max}; long instruction files get followed less
doctor.memory.fix_too_long: Move details out of {file} into docs or skills until it has at most {max} lines, or raise memory.maxLines in .finitemonkey/config.yml
doctor.git.autocrlf: git converts line endings to CRLF on checkout (core.autocrlf=true) and {file} does not pin LF; shell hooks and scripts checked out with CRLF fail with "bad interpreter"
doctor.git.fix_autocrlf: add `* text=auto eol=lf` to {file}, commit it, then run `git add --renormalize .`
history.title: Looking back at this project's local Claude Code sessions: {sessions, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}}, {turns, plural, one {# turn} other {# turns}}.
history.pattern.done_after_failing_tests: {count, plural, one {# turn} other {# turns}} ended with "done" right after a failing test run
history.pattern.env_read: {count, plural, one {# read} other {# reads}} of a .env file
history.pattern.no_verify: {count, plural, one {# git command} other {# git commands}} with --no-verify
history.pattern.force_push: {count, plural, one {# force push} other {# force pushes}}
history.pattern.test_skip: {count, plural, one {# test edit} other {# test edits}} that added .skip, .only or a skip marker
history.estimate: These are estimates from pattern matching, not evidence; nothing was saved and nothing left this machine.
gate.require.review: a reviewer subagent read the change at its current state
gate.size.declared: size {effective}: {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}, {lines, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}
gate.size.grew: declared {declared}, the diff makes it {effective}: {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}, {lines, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}
gate.review.missing: no review of the current state: run a reviewer subagent on the diff, or the person writes `fm: approve {check} <reason>` in the chat
secrets.warn.write: Finite Monkey warning (the write went through): {found}. A secret passed as a command-line argument shows in ps and docker inspect; disabled TLS verification lets anyone on the path read the traffic. Move the value to an environment variable or a secret file, and keep TLS checks on outside tests.
doctor.secrets.remote_credential: git remote {remotes} has a credential in its URL, stored in plain text in .git/config
doctor.secrets.fix_remote_credential: run `git remote set-url {remote} <url without user:token@>`, use a credential helper or SSH, and rotate the token
secrets.session.remote_credential: git remote {remotes} has a credential in its URL (plain text in .git/config). Ask the person to run `git remote set-url {remote} <url without user:token@>` and rotate the token; do not print the URL.
gate.require.callers: no removed or renamed symbol is still called
gate.callers.none: {count, plural, one {# removed definition} other {# removed definitions}}, no caller left
gate.callers.open: {name} is gone but still called in {count, plural, one {# place} other {# places}}
gate.callers.warning: warning only: {percent}% of callers findings were released with callers_ignore ({released} of {total}), above the 5% ceiling
command.policy_false_positive.summary: Record a false positive of a guard in shadow so it is not promoted
policy.error.person_only: Only the person can record a false positive, and this does not look like their terminal (no TTY, or running inside Claude Code)
policy.false_positive.recorded: Recorded for {guard}: {count, plural, one {# false positive} other {# false positives}}; it stays in shadow until you set it in .finitemonkey/policy.yml.
command.app_check.summary: Start the app or reuse the running one, call one route and check the answer
app.check.crashed: the app exited with code {code} before opening the port
app.check.no_port: the port of {url} did not open before the timeout
app.check.no_start: nothing listens on {url} and no start command was given
app.check.usage: give --port as a number from 1 to 65535; --status and --timeout must be positive numbers
gate.require.runtime: the app starts and `{command}` answers as declared
gate.runtime.crashed: the app exited with code {code} before opening its port
gate.runtime.no_port: port {port} did not open before the timeout
gate.runtime.no_start: nothing listens on port {port} and the check has no `run` to start the app
gate.runtime.orphan: the app on port {port} could not be stopped
gate.runtime.probe_failed: the app check did not report a result: {line}
command.off.summary: Pause the gate and warnings for the current Claude Code session (the person only)
command.on.summary: Resume the gate after fm off
pause.off: Gate paused for this session by the person. Secrets, production and destructive git guards stay on. Type `fm on` to resume.
pause.report: The gate did not check this stop: the person paused it with fm off at {since}.
pause.no_session: No Claude Code session is recorded for this project yet; start one, then run this again or type `fm off` there.
pause.error.person_only: Only the person can pause or resume the gate, and this does not look like their terminal (no TTY, or running inside Claude Code)
secrets.command.live: Check whether a key still works with its provider (off by default; sends only with --send, and prints the host first)
secrets.action.live: send a key to its provider
secrets.live.dry: Nothing was sent. With --send, the value of ${variable} would go to {host} ({url}) to check whether the {provider} key still works. Run it yourself, in your own terminal, with --send.
secrets.live.contacting: Contacting {host} ({url}) with the key; the value is passed to curl on stdin, never as an argument.
secrets.live.live: The key in ${variable} still works at {host} (HTTP {status}). Revoke it now: see the runbook in `finitemonkey secrets incident`.
secrets.live.rejected: {host} rejected the key in ${variable} (HTTP {status}): it no longer works.
secrets.live.unknown: {host} answered HTTP {status}; that does not say whether the key in ${variable} works. Check it in the provider's console.
secrets.live.unreachable: Could not reach {host} with curl, so the key in ${variable} was not checked.
secrets.live.no_value: ${variable} is empty or not set in this terminal; export it first, nothing was sent
githooks.command.commit_msg: Check a commit message: Conventional Commits header and no AI attribution (for the commit-msg git hook)
githooks.command.push_check: Check what a push sends: secrets, commit messages, merges that dropped lines and protected branches (for the pre-push git hook)
githooks.command.ci_gate: Run the same checks on a pull request's commits in CI, one line per failing check with its fix
githooks.error.failed: {count, plural, one {# check failed} other {# checks failed}}
githooks.error.no_base: the base {detail} does not exist here; fetch it first (actions/checkout needs fetch-depth: 0)
command.look.summary: Capture the screens in .finitemonkey/look.yml at 1440 and 390 px and measure them
look.done: {count, plural, one {# capture} other {# captures}}, {failures, plural, one {# failure} other {# failures}}. Open every capture with Read.
look.error.not_a_repo: look runs inside a git repository
look.error.not_configured: .finitemonkey/look.yml is missing or has no port
look.error.playwright_missing: Playwright is not installed in this project
look.error.browser_missing: no Chromium, Chrome or Edge could be started
look.error.app_failed: the app did not come up: {detail}
gate.require.look: changed screens captured with zero failures and every capture opened after the last edit
gate.look.not_run: no capture of the current tree: run `finitemonkey look`
gate.look.no_captures: the last look run produced no capture
gate.look.allow_ignored: exception ignored, its decision is not recorded: {entry}
gate.look.unopened: {count, plural, one {# capture} other {# captures}} not opened after the last edit to a screen file
gate.look.ok: {count, plural, one {# capture} other {# captures}}, no failure, all opened
reason.human.generic: Blocked a tool call; the reason went to Claude.
review.command.packet: Print the review packet for the reviewer and verifier agents: diff, task contract, evidence ledger and REVIEW.md, never the conversation
review.guard.read_only: blocked: the {agent} agent is read-only and cannot use {tool}. Report the finding; the main session makes the change.
review.error.no_base: the base {detail} is not a commit here
command.statusline.summary: Print the status line: active task, gate state and context use
command.gain.summary: What the guards did: saves next to false alarms and gate failures
gain.title: Finite Monkey, last {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} (from .finitemonkey/log.jsonl and the evidence ledgers):
gain.row.blocks: {count, plural, one {# block} other {# blocks}} by the guards
gain.row.saves: {count, plural, one {# block} other {# blocks}} followed by a green gate within a day
gain.row.false_positives: {count, plural, one {# false alarm} other {# false alarms}} (releases typed by the person, and false positives recorded)
gain.row.gate_runs: {count, plural, one {# gate run} other {# gate runs}}
gain.row.gate_failed: {count, plural, one {# gate run} other {# gate runs}} failed
gain.row.gate_unverified: {count, plural, one {# gate run} other {# gate runs}} ended not verified
gain.row.gate_time: {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} spent in the gate
gain.footer: Counts come from local files only; a save is a block followed by a passing gate, not proof that the block caused it.
critique.command.verify: Check a review's must-fix findings: run each reproduction command on base and head in throwaway worktrees and keep only what fails on head alone
critique.title: Critique
critique.demoted: Finding {id} was marked must fix without a reproduction command and expected result, so it counts as should fix.
critique.decision: Decision needed: finding {id} ({what}) already fails on the base branch and is an active risk.
critique.error.invalid: the findings file is not valid: {detail}
critique.error.must_fix: {count, plural, one {# must-fix finding reproduced on head only} other {# must-fix findings reproduced on head only}}
install.warn.sandbox_offer: The Claude Code sandbox runs here. Add --sandbox to turn it on for you only, in .claude/settings.local.json: it fails to start without the sandbox, hides ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and .env files from commands, and lets them reach only the hosts in sandbox.hosts.
install.warn.sandbox_unsupported: --sandbox was ignored: native Windows has no Claude Code sandbox, so the guards are the only protection here. Run Claude Code inside WSL2 to use it.
gate.guard.rewrite.claim: the command that ran is not the one Finite Monkey checked; another hook rewrote it (checked: `{checked}`; ran: `{ran}`)
gate.guard.rewrite.requires: a sensitive command runs exactly as it was checked; find the hook that rewrites it and stop it from changing this command
gate.guard.rewrite.not: a rewrite that looks equivalent, or running the same command again through the same hook
gate.guard.rewrite.human: Another hook changed a sensitive command after Finite Monkey checked it; both versions are in .finitemonkey/log.jsonl.
doctor.hooks.rewriters: {hooks, plural, one {# other hook sees} other {# other hooks see}} shell commands before they run and can rewrite them ({list}); a sensitive command they change fails the gate
doctor.hooks.fix_rewriters: If a hook rewrites commands (updatedInput), make it skip git, rm, ssh, kubectl and .env commands, or remove it
deps.warn.header: Check these new packages before installing them (a warning, nothing was blocked):
deps.warn.human: {count, plural, one {# warning about a new package} other {# warnings about new packages}}; see the details before installing.
deps.finding.missing: {name} does not exist on {registry}; the name may be made up.
deps.finding.typo: {name} is one or two letters away from the popular package {popular}; check the spelling.
deps.finding.young: {name} has little history: first published {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago, {count, plural, one {# version} other {# versions}}.
deps.finding.fresh: {name}@{version} was published {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}} ago; prefer a version at least {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} old.
deps.finding.script: {name}@{version} adds an install script that the previous version did not have; read it before installing.
deps.finding.unchecked: {name} was not checked on {registry} (offline or no answer in time), so only the spelling was checked.
creds.command.inventory: Write .finitemonkey/creds.yml: every credential the project reads, where, in which environments, its type and risk (names only)
creds.block.static.claim: {file} would read the static cloud key {variable} from secrets, and {provider} accepts OIDC from GitHub Actions
creds.block.static.requires: Use the short-lived login instead: {alternative}. If the project truly needs the static key, ask the person to record an exception
creds.block.not: the same key under another secret name, or passed through env or a script
creds.block.human: Kept the static cloud key {variable} out of {file}: {provider} accepts OIDC.
creds.inventory.written: {count, plural, one {# credential} other {# credentials}} written to {file} (names only).
creds.inventory.shared: {name} is read by {services}; a rotation has to reach all of them at once.
creds.inventory.static_cloud: {name} is a static {cloud} key; prefer OIDC where the provider accepts it.
creds.inventory.incident: {file} was committed in {commit}; incident {id} is open until the values in it are rotated.
env.unignored: {file} is not ignored by git; only .env.example belongs in the repository.
env.public: {name} ({where}) has a public prefix and a secret-like name; the bundler ships it to every browser.
env.undocumented: {name} is read at {where} but is missing from .env.example.
env.unused: {name} is in {file} but no code reads it.
env.history: .env file {file} is in the git history (commit {commit}).
env.fix_unignored: Add `.env*` and `!.env.example` to .gitignore, and `git rm --cached` the file if it is tracked.
env.fix_public: Drop the public prefix and read the value on the server only.
env.fix_parity: Keep .env.example listing every variable the code reads, with empty or fake values.
env.fix_history: Run `finitemonkey creds` to open the incident, rotate every value the file held, then close it.
